newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service bill vote seen postponed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service bill vote seen postponed.

text.p: Brazilian political leaders gathered to discuss the possibility of putting the government's civil service reform to a first lower house vote Wednesday.
But a deputy who drew up the bill said there was little chance the vote would take place because many lawmakers were divided over a proposed pay ceiling that would hit their income.
"It will probably have to wait until the week after Easter," deputy Wellington Moreira Franco told reporters.

The government has so far failed to overcome resistance in Congress to a proposed 10,800 real ($10,285) ceiling on pay and benefits for public sector workers and pensioners included in its civil service reform bill.

An estimated 140 members of the 513-strong Chamber of Deputies stand to lose out under the ceiling because they currently earn handsome pensions from previous public-sector posts on top of their 8,000 real monthly salaries.
As a constitutional amendment, the civil service reform requires two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress.
It is considered an important tool in the government's efforts to rein in public spending.
